extracted.intended_audience: Judge Advocates General, military legal officers, Army commanders, and administrative officers applying Army regulations
extracted.subtask_description: A compiled digest of legal opinions of the Judge Advocates General of the U.S. Army (1862–1912) giving rules, interpretations, and administrative standards on matters such as absence, leaves, furloughs, passes, and related personnel administration. The document records citation practice and organization conventions for locating opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and synopsis conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Subjects in the Digest are arranged alphabetically. Divisions of a Subject are indicated by Roman numerals, subdivisions by capital letters, Arabic numerals, small bold-faced letters, parentheses, brackets and other ordered devices; each paragraph is preceded by characters which indicate its place in the synopsis. Opinions of the Judge Advocate General's Office are cited shorthand (C. for Cards, P. for Letter Press Books, R. for Record Books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the documented hierarchy (I, A, 1, a, (1), (a), [1], [a], [A]) when locating or cross-referencing opinions. Paragraph prefix characters are the canonical locator. Citations use the office shorthand (C., P., R.). Many Subjects are cross-references only; minimize repetition of locator characters in cross-reference lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave of absence is discretionary (an indulgence) not a legal right
rubrics_metrics.description: A leave of absence is an indulgence which is or may be granted to an officer at the pleasure and in the discretion of a proper military superior; it is not a privilege created by law and therefore can never be demanded as a matter of legal right. (C. 13346, Dec. 8, 1903)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat applications for leave as discretionary administrative acts; do not interpret entitlement-based statutes to create a common-law right to ordinary discretionary leaves. Decisions denying leave on discretion are supported by precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave and duty status are mutually exclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: The status of leave of absence and that of duty are incompatible and both cannot exist at the same time with respect to the same person; if one exists the other necessarily ceases to exist. When conflicting orders arise, the superior authority (e.g., Secretary of War) supersedes the inferior (e.g., commanding general). (C. 20917; 23666)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two authorities create conflicting statuses for an officer, the status created by the higher authority prevails. Do not attempt to treat an officer as both 'on leave' and 'on duty' simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability incurred while on leave is not pensionable line-of-duty disability
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer disabled while on leave does not, by that fact, occupy a status of duty; disability must be incurred in the line of duty to be pensionable. (C. 25634; 19323)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pension/line-of-duty determinations, establish whether the disabling event occurred in the line of duty. Disability sustained while on leave generally is not a basis for pension unless other facts show line-of-duty nexus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to grant leave — limits and non-retroactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Post and other commanders have defined authority to grant leaves; they may extend leaves within their power but may not grant leaves nunc pro tunc (retroactively). Certain officers (e.g., Chief of Engineers) are not 'department commanders' and lack authority to grant leaves in that capacity. (C. 17491; 17440; 21294)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant leaves prospectively only. Verify regulatory delegation of leave-granting authority for each class of commander; do not assume authority where statute/regulation limits it. Extensions are permissible when within the grantor's authority but retrospective creation of leave is impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaves to be stated in months and days; days cannot be converted into months
rubrics_metrics.description: Army Regulations require 'leaves of absence will be granted in terms of months and days.' If a leave less than a month is extended for specific days, there is no authority to convert the total into months: measure leave in the terms granted. (C. 19284)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute and record leave in the exact units granted. Avoid administrative conversion between units which would alter the leave's legal character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave order does not automatically relieve from duty; post commander must ensure relief
rubrics_metrics.description: An order granting leave of absence does not by its proprio vigore relieve an officer from duty at his post; the post commander must ensure a successor is appointed for money/property accountability and that special duties are covered. (C. 18756)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When granting leave, verify that the post commander has arranged appropriate relief and accountability transfers. Administrative processes must ensure continuity of obligations notwithstanding leave orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff officers' leaves over one month require War Department action
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for leaves of absence for staff officers for more than one month must be forwarded to the War Department so that the head of the staff department can consider replacement, bonded status, tour closings, and other administrative consequences. (Par. 51, Army Regulations; C. 17037)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route leave applications for staff officers exceeding one month to central authority. Consider replacement availability, bonding, and operational impact before approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special/leaves for academy and service-school academic staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1330 R.S. and the act of March 23, 1910, professors, assistant professors and instructors at the Military Academy and at service schools may be granted leaves for suspension of academic duties; such leave must be taken during the leave year in which it accrues, is not cumulative, and may be taken at other times during the academic year if services can be spared. (C. 27492; C. 17388; C. 18286)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply statutory special-leave provisions to academic staff (including veterinarians on academic duty). Do not extend the benefit to student officers or those whose duty is post-only unless expressly provided. Require that such leaves be charged to the year of accrual and enforce noncumulativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hunting leave treated as ordinary leave unless explicitly for Government convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Although hunting leaves were previously treated as special expeditions, circular No. 35 (July 26, 1905) and subsequent decisions hold that authorized absences except for sickness or wounds count as absence with leave unless shown to be for the convenience of the Government; thus hunting leaves must be shown to be for the convenience of the Government or else are ordinary leaves. (C. 18487)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When granting hunting leave, include an explicit statement if the leave is for the convenience of the Government to avoid classification as ordinary leave. Otherwise apply ordinary-leave rules and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary pass protections and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A pass authorizes brief absence and serves as both authority for temporary absence within the garrison and protection against molestation while outside the post so long as express or implied conditions are not violated. There is no vested right in a pass; it may be revoked. A pass cannot be used to cover desertion or as protection beyond its time/place limits. (C. 1397; 23666; 2658; 29211)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define pass terms (place and hour) clearly; enforce its revocability; treat misuse (e.g., traveling further than permitted or using pass to separate from service) as absence without leave or desertion. Report and record pass revocations and violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass vs. furlough — substance over form (duration and status determine character)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pass is an instrument authorizing brief absence without removing a man from the list 'present for duty' and should be restricted to the vicinity of the post and not over 24 hours. If an instrument called a 'pass' authorizes several days and travel to a considerable distance, it should be treated as a 'furlough' regardless of its name. (C. 24293; 23666; 15841)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify absence instruments by their practical effect: duration and created status. Do not rely on the document's label; treat multi-day, distant-authority permits as furloughs and apply furlough rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furloughs: commander's discretion and employment while on furlough
rubrics_metrics.description: A furlough is within the regimental commander's exclusive jurisdiction where law/regulation so provides and his discretion is not subject to revision by higher authority if within that jurisdiction. An enlisted man on furlough may be employed by the Quartermaster's Department or accept employment in civil life; uniform need not be worn. (C. 15841; C. 2607; C. 5005; C. 5408)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adjudicating furlough requests, determine jurisdictional boundaries for review. Approve employment while on furlough unless statute/regulation prohibits. Do not require uniform while on furlough absent regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays in reporting after furlough — government-caused delays may be excused
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier on furlough applied timely for transportation but the Government delayed furnishing it and the soldier therefore reported late, the period between expiration of furlough and actual reporting may be excused by proper authority and commutation of rations will not be forfeited. If the soldier has been discharged, delay cannot be excused. (G. 3988; C. 7020)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When late reporting is due to government delay, exercise discretion to excuse delay and preserve pay/commutation where appropriate. Do not excuse delays after discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment of leave may be express or implied
rubrics_metrics.description: Relinquishment is express when made in writing (requiring acceptance by proper superior authority) and implied when the officer reports at his proper post or other designated post before the leave expiration. (C. 27846)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require written relinquishment forms for express surrender of leave where formal acceptance is necessary. Recognize early return to post as implied relinquishment and adjust records accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutation of quarters and allowances during leave under statutory leave provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act of July 29, 1876, officers entitled to leaves 'without deduction of pay or allowance' are also entitled to commutation of quarters and allowances where applicable; the term 'allowance' denotes emoluments distinct from pay. (P. U. 271; E. 44)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating pay and allowances during leaves authorized by statute, include commutation of quarters and other allowances distinct from pay unless statute states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of arrival in the United States for statutory purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the act of March 2, 1901, the 'date of arrival in the United States' is when the transport has reached the terminus of its voyage — i.e., the dock where passengers and cargo can be discharged. (C. 18286; 25592)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ship/dock arrival time as the operative statutory date, not earlier anchorings or estimated times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return transportation charges for enlisted men on furlough from overseas possessions
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlisted man on furlough in the United States from an overseas possession who requests return transportation and is given an order for transportation on a commercial liner should be charged for such transportation against his pay; post commander's order does not carry government-paid commercial liner transportation in such a case. (C. 27100)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arranging return travel for enlisted men from furlough in the U.S., verify whether government transport is available; if only commercial transport is used by order, charge cost to soldier unless regulation/statute provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nurses' leave entitlement and noncumulativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 19 of the act of February 2, 1901 provides nurses may be granted leaves of absence for 30 days with pay for each calendar year; nurses appointed under the act are part of the U.S. Army (not civilian employees) and may not be granted cumulative leaves. (C. 10160; C. 10160 May 31, 1902)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat nurses appointed under the statute as military personnel for leave/pay rules. Enforce the 30-days-per-calendar-year limit and disallow accumulation of unused leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to excuse absence without leave rests with leave-granting authority (or next higher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1265 R.S., the power to decide whether an officer's absence in excess of a leave is excused as unavoidable vests in the officer who is empowered to grant the leave; if the absence exceeds that commander's power, the authority to excuse passes to the next higher commander whose conclusions are final unless appealed. (C. 20764)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route overstay-excuse determinations through the chain of command to the officer who could grant the leave, or higher if necessary. Treat such determinations as discretionary and final absent appeal.
